hold_text: Routed for a human merge because R5 cannot certify src/** as Tier-1, NOT because the work is reclassified. The approval sought is a manager/operator MERGE of a Tier-1 read-path change; no Tier-2/3 permission is being requested and none is needed for anything in this diff. Reviewer's check is one question: does this diff touch a WRITER, an ORDER PATH, or a CONFIG? It does not -- the only src/ change is the SELECT/JOIN construction inside src/web/api/routers/performance.py, a read endpoint.
why: MI-144 post-deploy follow-up. PR #11131 deployed at 15:05Z and, checked against the pre-merge measurement rather than accepted, its bracketOutcome block was found to grade only 23.1% of the real-money book: it joins order_packages on trades.order_package_id alone, and MEASURED on the live journal only 120 of 470 real-money closed non-backtest rows (25.5%) carry one. 325 of the 350 NULL rows are reachable via the reverse edge order_packages.linked_trade_id, lifting coverage to 420 of 428 (98.1%) and the published answer from 44/99 (44.4%) to 228/420 (54.3%). Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list -- 'observability / read paths, retrieving + analyzing state'. NO journal writer, NO order path, NO config/**, NO risk caps, NO deploy/ or unit file. Nothing in it can place, modify, or refuse an order. The fallback is consulted ONLY where the forward key is NULL, so it cannot change a package a row already resolved, and it is pre-aggregated with MIN(order_package_id) so it cannot fan out and double-count a trade -- linked_trade_id is unique across all 4436 packages today (1113 over 1113 distinct trades), so that guard is defensive rather than load-bearing, written while the data happens to be kind. Two of the three new tests were VERIFIED failing without the change; the third is a regression pin that cannot discriminate and is labelled as such. Effect on R is stated rather than implied: the same join moves rBasis.declaredInitial 103->106 and expectancyR -0.3152 -> -0.3153, because reverse-linked packages carry sl/tp but rarely a meta.risk_per_unit.
